source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar, §11.9 Reduced verb forms; Martin Orwin, Colloquial Somali, reduced verb forms
rule: For ordinary suffixing verbs under subject focus, the affirmative simple-present reduced paradigm has three forms. The default form serves 1sg/2sg/3sg_m/2pl/3pl, 3sg_f keeps t-marking, and 1pl keeps n-marking. The final present vowel is short -a rather than full-paradigm -aa.

source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar, §11.9; Martin Orwin, Colloquial Somali
rule: The affirmative present-progressive reduced paradigm likewise has three forms: default 1sg/2sg/3sg_m/2pl/3pl, distinct 3sg_f, and distinct 1pl. The final full-paradigm -aa is shortened to -a.

source: Svolacchia, Mereu & Puglielli, Aspects of Discourse Configurationality in Somali; Saeed examples cited in Dalrymple & Nikolaeva
rule: A focused subject uses reduced agreement; the full 3pl progressive form is not licensed merely because the focused subject is plural.

source: Martin Orwin, Colloquial Somali; Morgan Nilsson, Somali grammar descriptions
rule: Known irregular/prefixing verbs have source-specific reduced present behavior. Relevant reviewed examples include imow: yimaadda/timaadda for default/feminine; aqaan: yaqaan/taqaan/naqaan; aal-yaal: yaal/taal/naal; and copular ahaw: invariant ah in absolutive reduced present. These are contextual focus forms and must not be promoted to an unrestricted global paradigm.
